requirement: Logging producers shall be able to submit JSON log messages over HTTP POST without requiring a language-specific client library. The server shall parse request bodies within the configured size limit and accept them for forwarding to browser clients.

Users shall be able to view incoming logs in a server-hosted browser interface. The server shall deliver each received log object to all connected display clients in real time through Socket.IO, with each browser connecting to the server that hosts its page.

The browser client shall validate each received log object against a data model requiring the logged data and a string display type. If validation fails, it shall present a displayable error containing the validation details and the original message instead of silently discarding the message.

The browser shall retain received logs and generated error entries in its current client-side state and display them through configured visualizers in the registered display windows. Users shall be able to filter log entries by tags and see variable-name annotations when that metadata is supplied.

The system shall allow visualizers to be added through configuration, use the user configuration when available and the default configuration otherwise, and render each log object with the first capable visualizer in configured order. Failure to load one visualizer shall not prevent other valid visualizers from loading.
Operators and logging clients shall be able to check whether the server is responding through a status request that returns an HTTP success response.

Operators shall be able to start the Node.js/Express server through the provided command-line or npm entry points and select its listening port. Startup shall display the browser client URL for the selected port and attempt to open it in the default browser.
